effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative estimates from bivariate comparisons, multivariable linear and logistic regressions, and GSEM mediation/path analysis on N = 593 households. Sanitation access also differed significantly between notified and non-notified neighbourhoods (open defecation 2.1% vs. 4.5%, home toilet 6.0% vs. 12.6%, pay community toilet 91.9% vs. 82.9%, p = 0.005; Table 1).
effect_estimate.value: In multivariable linear regression adjusting for household size, monthly per capita income and religion (N = 593), non-notified households used 37.3% fewer litres per capita per day (LPCD) of water than notified households (95% CI: -46.4% to -26.5%, p < 0.001; unadjusted difference: -38.2%, p < 0.001; median 17.7 LPCD [IQR 10.7–34.1] vs. 31.4 LPCD [IQR 17.6–51.7], p < 0.0001). In multivariable logistic regression, non-notified households had 3.4 times higher adjusted odds of consuming <=20 LPCD. Non-notified households also had lower primary access to in-home taps (2.6% vs. 9.9%, p < 0.001), paid higher median water costs (407 vs. 219 INR/1,000 L; median 11% [IQR 6–20] vs. 9% [IQR 5–17] of monthly household income, p = 0.01), obtained water less frequently (<3 times/week: 49.0% vs. 26.5%, p < 0.001), had more days with insufficient water, and were more likely to miss or be late for work due to water collection (30.3% vs. 22.6%, p = 0.03). In GSEM path analysis, water source infrastructure, accessibility, reliability and cost mediated 38.7% of the association between non-notified status and LPCD (direct unmediated difference: -23.4%).

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 by the analytical cross-sectional design ceiling (JBI tool). Assigned 2 because the study directly observes and documents the legal-administrative mechanism on the ground—combining analysis of statutory notification and pre-2000 documentation rules under the Maharashtra Slum Areas Act 1971, census GIS mapping showing spatial non-extension and non-functionality of municipal community water taps in the non-notified neighbourhood, and household GSEM path analysis tracing how municipal infrastructure exclusion drives vendor/tanker reliance, crowding, cost, unreliability and lower LPCD.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines legal slum notification/recognition and security of tenure under the Maharashtra Slum Areas Act 1971 (tenure), pre-2000 residence proof such as voter ID cards (documentation), exclusion of central government/private land vs. state/municipal land (property), neighbourhood-level infrastructure boundaries excluding non-notified areas (service_area), group tap application hurdles for dispersed eligible households (procedural_steps), and municipal officials' administrative discretion and neighbourhood-level stereotyping in service approvals (discretion).

outcome_flags.comment: Measures in-home taps and municipal community piped taps (formal_connection), primary/secondary water sources and collection time/crowding (water_access), household sanitation method (sanitation_access), GIS spatial coverage of functional community taps within 10m radius (service_coverage), weekly frequency of water delivery and scheduled pressure (service_reliability), LPCD and days with insufficient water (service_quantity), unit water price and share of household income spent on water (affordability), and intermittent supply/tap functionality status (service_continuity). Microbiological water quality was explicitly not measured.

sample_size.comment: 600 households were randomly selected from a complete census enumeration (1,285 households in Matangrushi Nagar and 918 in Indira Nagar); 7 lacked key water variables, yielding N = 593 households in the analytic sample, alongside GIS mapping of public community taps across both neighbourhoods.
sample_size.value: 593 households analysed across 2 neighbourhoods (283 notified households in Matangrushi Nagar and 310 non-notified households in Indira Nagar), out of 600 randomly sampled households surveyed

study_design.comment: Data collected March–May 2016 via two-week container enumeration household survey and GPS/GIS tap mapping; authors explicitly note in Section IV that data are cross-sectional and cannot establish causality.
study_design.value: Cross-sectional representative household survey and GIS infrastructure mapping with multivariable linear and logistic regression and generalized structural equation modelling (GSEM) path analysis
